nodes.label: Hover-only interactive UI with zero focus and ARIA states
nodes.norm_label: hover-only interactive ui with zero focus and aria states
nodes.rationale: The audit's central finding: 'No `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, `outline` in `index.astro`, `SocialIcons.astro`, `track-render.ts`, `custom.css` (verified via grep). Keyboard = browser default only.' [file:L2500] The same grep covered ARIA and found 'No `aria-*`, `role`, `tabindex`, `alt`, `aria-current`, skip-link' [file:L2506], and the interactive elements are links styled as buttons with hover-only rules [file:L2474].
nodes.summary: A production-readiness audit of the real (non-docs) UI surface in apps/learn found that every interactive element is an anchor with a hover rule and nothing else: no focus-visible outline, no active or disabled state, and no ARIA anywhere. Keyboard users get browser defaults only.

nodes.label: SSR HTML routes return JSON error bodies instead of HTML pages
nodes.norm_label: ssr html routes return json error bodies instead of html pages
nodes.rationale: The audit records that a bad slug on the tracks route 'returns JSON `{error:not_found}` 404, not HTML page' [file:L2491] and the skills route has the 'same JSON 404' [file:L2492]. A browser navigation to a nonexistent track URL therefore lands on a raw JSON body rather than any page carrying recovery links.
nodes.summary: The two server-rendered content routes answer a missing slug with a JSON `{error: not_found}` payload and a 404 status. Nothing renders an HTML error document, so the user sees a bare JSON body with no navigation and no recovery path.

nodes.label: Gate rejections redirect to login without a reason parameter
nodes.norm_label: gate rejections redirect to login without a reason parameter
nodes.rationale: All five gate failure paths in middleware.ts — no cookie, no D1 binding, D1 query error, expired session, unentitled plan — 'bare 302 to login, no `?reason`, user gets login loop with no feedback' [file:L2494]. The console logs carry the reject reason but the redirect does not, so the distinction is invisible to the person being redirected.
nodes.summary: Five distinct rejection causes collapse into the same bare 302 to the login route with no reason query parameter. The middleware logs the cause server-side, but a user who lacks entitlement and a user whose D1 binding is missing are indistinguishable at the redirect.

nodes.label: The 404 page covers only prerendered docs, not SSR routes
nodes.norm_label: the 404 page covers only prerendered docs, not ssr routes
nodes.rationale: The written 404 page is good — localized copy plus three recovery links — but it 'Covers prerendered Starlight docs only; does not cover SSR `/app/*`, `/tracks/*`, `/skills/*`' [file:L2497]. The boundary that makes this unavoidable is stated in the code the audit read: prerendered assets are 'served before the worker runs, so only SSR surfaces can be gated' [file:L614], and the funnel pages 'cannot be gated here. Only SSR' surfaces pass through middleware [file:L1215]. The SSR surfaces are exactly the ones with no HTML 404.
nodes.summary: The localized 404 document exists and is well made, but Starlight resolves it from the prerendered docs collection, so every server-rendered surface under /app, /tracks and /skills has no HTML error page at all.

nodes.label: Hardcoded hex colors bypass the design tokens and leave contrast unverified
nodes.norm_label: hardcoded hex colors bypass the design tokens and leave contrast unverified
nodes.rationale: Contrast is verified only in the token file, which 'claims AA (dark 6.18:1, light 5.18:1) for accent tokens' [file:L2509]. The components then hardcode '`#e8e9eb/#17181c`, `#ff6a00`, `#ffa25c` (not tokens, unverified)' [file:L2510], and track-render.ts adds `color-scheme:dark` with no light-theme path, so the verified ratios do not describe what the pages actually paint.
nodes.summary: WCAG AA ratios were computed once for the Starlight accent tokens, but the member dashboard and the SSR track template hardcode their own hex values instead of referencing those tokens, and the track template declares dark scheme only. The verified numbers therefore do not cover the colors users see.

nodes.label: RSS double-counts shared pages across a browser process tree; PSS is the real number
nodes.norm_label: rss double-counts shared pages across a browser process tree; pss is the real number
rationale: Task managers showed 1.248 MB of RSS [file:L04713] against a measured PSS of 490 MB [file:L4745]; the gap is 'Selisih (memori di-double-count) | **758 MB** | Pustaka/framework dibagi antar 12 proses' [file:L4746]. Firefox runs as twelve processes loading the same libraries, so summing RSS counts those pages once per process and roughly doubles the apparent figure.
nodes.summary: Summing RSS over a twelve-process Firefox tree counts every shared library page once per process. Reading Pss from smaps_rollup per process instead gives the honest contribution to physical RAM, which on this machine was 874 MB at peak against 1693 MB of summed RSS.

nodes.label: mozLz4 session store files carry a twelve-byte header before the LZ4 block
nodes.rationale: Decoding failed at every guessed offset with 'bad offset 8690 at dst 7' until the byte layout was read off the file: 'header appears to be 12 bytes: "mozLz4\0\0" (8) + 4-byte LE size ... Then block starts at 12' [file:L931]. With the body set to raw[12:] the store decoded cleanly — 'Header-nya 12 byte (magic + ukuran), blok LZ4 mulai di offset 12' [file:L985] — and reported 1 to 2 tabs, refuting the many-open-tabs theory outright.
nodes.summary: Firefox session store .jsonlz4 files are an eight-byte magic followed by a four-byte little-endian uncompressed size, so the raw LZ4 block begins at offset twelve. Decoders that assume the classic eight-byte magic fail with a nonsensical offset error.

nodes.label: Copying the profile and toggling extensions in extensions.json isolates their memory cost
nodes.norm_label: copying the profile and toggling extensions in extensions.json isolates their memory cost
nodes.rationale: The control ran on a throwaway copy: non-builtin addons were rewritten to active=false and userDisabled=true ('ekstensi dinonaktifkan: 7' [file:L3893]) and the copy launched with --no-remote on its own port, leaving the real profile untouched. Measured against a clean-profile baseline of 475 MB [file:L4754], the user's profile with extensions off cost 490 MB [file:L4755] and with extensions on 523 MB — 'Ekstensi = +33 MB' [file:L4756].
nodes.summary: To attribute Firefox memory without touching the live profile, copy it, rewrite each addon's active and userDisabled flags in extensions.json, and run the copy as a separate --no-remote instance at about:blank. Comparing PSS across three such instances measured eight extensions at 33 MB.

nodes.label: Tab weight, not extension count, drives Firefox RAM
nodes.norm_label: tab weight, not extension count, drives firefox ram
nodes.rationale: Opening one YouTube tab moved total PSS by '+649 MB untuk satu tab' [file:L5052] and WhatsApp Web added '+883 MB' [file:L5129], while all eight extensions together accounted for 33 MB [file:L4756]. The session store held only one or two tabs, so the usual 'too many tabs' explanation did not hold — the sites themselves are the cost, and a single SPA tab outweighs the entire extension set.
nodes.summary: Measured on one machine: baseline Firefox is about 475 MB, eight third-party extensions add 33 MB, and individual heavy web apps add 650 to 880 MB each. The perceived RAM hunger tracks which sites are open, not how many extensions are installed.

nodes.label: Unload Tab discards a tab's content process while keeping the tab
nodes.norm_label: unload tab discards a tab's content process while keeping the tab
nodes.rationale: Verified in Firefox's own omni.ja rather than assumed: '`browser.tabs.unloadTabInContextMenu` default true → klik kanan tab → "Unload Tab" (menu `context_unloadTab`)' [file:L7347], alongside an about:unloads page and `browser.tabs.unloadOnLowMemory` default true, which already discards tabs under memory pressure [file:L7350]. The note is explicit that this mechanism was not itself measured, only confirmed to exist in source.
nodes.summary: Right-clicking a tab and choosing Unload Tab, or using about:unloads, releases that tab's content process while the tab stays in the strip and reloads on click. Firefox also discards tabs automatically when memory runs low, so this is the built-in lever for the per-tab cost measured in this session.

nodes.label: Firefox's remote debugging port exposes BiDi with no way to create a session
nodes.norm_label: firefox's remote debugging port exposes bidi with no way to create a session
nodes.rationale: Every route to automation dead-ended. POST /session was refused with 'The handshake request must use GET method' [file:L2075] because that path is a WebSocket upgrade endpoint, CDP's /json/list returned 404, and connecting to the BiDi WebSocket and issuing browsingContext.getTree produced 'ERR "invalid session id"' [file:L2227]. BiDi commands require a session minted by the classic WebDriver HTTP endpoint, which this port does not serve, so per-tab attribution had to come from process RSS instead.
nodes.summary: On Firefox 156, --remote-debugging-port offers WebDriver BiDi over a WebSocket but no classic WebDriver endpoint, so no session can be created and every BiDi command fails with invalid session id. CDP HTTP routes are gone as well, leaving per-tab memory attribution dependent on out-of-process measurement.

nodes.label: Profile copies under /tmp consume the RAM being measured when /tmp is tmpfs
nodes.norm_label: profile copies under /tmp consume the ram being measured when /tmp is tmpfs
nodes.rationale: The control profiles were copied into /tmp, which on this machine is RAM-backed: '/tmp di mesin ini adalah **tmpfs (RAM)** — salinan profil saya tadi ikut makan RAM' [file:L4103]. The 772 MB of profile copies then pushed swap up, and the note records that 'Swap naik ke 1.078 MB — itu akibat salinan profil saya memenuhi tmpfs' [file:L4777]. The measurement scaffolding inflated the very number being measured until the copies were deleted.
nodes.summary: Copying a 764 MB browser profile into /tmp on a machine where /tmp is tmpfs spends real RAM on the experiment. Three such copies alongside two live instances distorted free-memory readings and drove over a gigabyte of swap before cleanup.
